facts.fact: Statewide gubernatorial campaigns may cover 6 to 15 media markets in larger states, including distinct urban and rural audiences.
facts.quote: Statewide campaigns may cover 6 to 15 media markets in larger states, including distinct urban and rural audiences.

facts.fact: Per AdWave, major metro DMAs typically deliver 40-65% of total state vote and dominate CTV inventory availability.
facts.quote: Major metros typically deliver 40-65% of total state vote and dominate CTV inventory availability.

facts.fact: Per AdWave, major metro DMAs lean CTV-heavy, with 60-75% of TV spend allocated to CTV.
facts.quote: Major metros lean CTV-heavy (60-75% of TV spend).

facts.fact: Per AdWave, mid-sized DMAs run a more balanced mix with CTV at 45-60% of TV spend, with broadcast and cable filling reach.
facts.quote: Mid-sized DMAs run more balanced (CTV 45-60%, with broadcast and cable filling reach).

facts.fact: Per AdWave, rural areas often need broadcast at 50-65% of TV spend, with CTV serving as a complement.
facts.quote: Rural areas often need broadcast 50-65% with CTV serving as a complement.

facts.fact: Per AdWave, Phase 1 (Introduction and contrast, May through Labor Day) recommended TV spend share is CTV 50-60%.
facts.quote: Recommended TV spend share: CTV 50-60%, broadcast 30-40%, cable 5-10% in this phase.

facts.fact: Per AdWave, Phase 2 (Persuasion, Labor Day through mid-October) recommended TV spend share is CTV 55-65%, broadcast 28-38%, and cable 5-10%.
facts.quote: Recommended TV spend share: CTV 55-65%, broadcast 28-38%, cable 5-10% in this phase.

facts.fact: Per AdWave, Phase 3 (Closing and mobilization, mid-October through Election Day) recommended TV spend share is CTV 50-60%, broadcast 35-45%, and cable 5-10%.
facts.quote: Recommended TV spend share: CTV 50-60%, broadcast 35-45%, cable 5-10% in this phase.

facts.fact: AdWave states that AI creative has cut spot production and traffic time from 7-14 days to 48-72 hours from script to air.
facts.quote: Spots that used to take 7-14 days to produce and traffic now go from script to air in 48-72 hours

facts.fact: Per AdWave, a modern statewide campaign typically operates with 4-6 persuasion universe segments.

facts.fact: Per Nielsen (as cited by AdWave), streaming overtook the combined viewing share of cable and broadcast for the first time in 2024.
facts.quote: Nielsen reported streaming overtaking the combined viewing share of cable and broadcast for the first time in 2024.

facts.fact: AdWave's recommended Phase 1 of a 2026 gubernatorial TV campaign runs from May through Labor Day.
facts.quote: Phase 1: Introduction and contrast (May through Labor Day)

facts.fact: AdWave's recommended Phase 2 of a 2026 gubernatorial TV campaign runs from Labor Day through mid-October.
facts.quote: Phase 2: Persuasion (Labor Day through mid-October)

facts.fact: AdWave describes the final three weeks (mid-October through Election Day) as the closing and mobilization phase of a gubernatorial TV campaign.
facts.quote: The final three weeks compress all of TV's strategic muscle.

facts.fact: Recommended frequency cap for gubernatorial CTV is 5-7 impressions per voter per week in the introduction phase, rising to 8-12 in closing weeks.
facts.quote: Lower caps (5-7 per voter per week) in introduction phase. Higher caps (8-12) in closing weeks as you push for recall.

facts.fact: Vendor benchmark for an open-seat race in a large competitive state with $40M+ total budget: TV typically $18M-$28M, with CTV at $9M-$16M (50-60% of TV).
facts.quote: **Open seat in a large competitive state with $40M+ total budget:** TV typically $18M-$28M, with CTV at $9M-$16M (50-60% of TV).

facts.fact: Vendor benchmark for a competitive race in a mid-sized state with $15M-$25M total budget: TV typically $7M-$13M, with CTV at $4M-$8M.
facts.quote: **Competitive race in mid-sized state with $15M-$25M total budget:** TV typically $7M-$13M, with CTV at $4M-$8M.

facts.fact: Vendor benchmark for a smaller-state competitive race with $5M-$12M total budget: TV typically $2.5M-$6M, with CTV at $1.4M-$3.5M.
facts.quote: **Smaller-state competitive race with $5M-$12M total budget:** TV typically $2.5M-$6M, with CTV at $1.4M-$3.5M.

facts.fact: For long-shot or safe-state races with under $3M total budget, vendor suggests TV under $1M with CTV at 70%+ of TV spend.
facts.quote: TV typically under $1M, with CTV at 70%+ of TV spend because of the efficiency advantage at smaller scale.

facts.fact: Gubernatorial total budgets range widely, with some races topping $100M in total spend and others running under $5M.
facts.quote: Gubernatorial budgets vary enormously, with some races topping $100M in total spend and others running under $5M.

facts.fact: Competitive 2024 gubernatorial campaigns reported CTV cost per persuaded voter of $25-$70, versus a typical $90-$180 for broadcast.
facts.quote: Competitive 2024 gubernatorial campaigns reported CTV costs per persuaded voter in the $25-$70 range, versus broadcast's typical $90-$180 range.

facts.fact: Vendor advises booking key CTV inventory windows by early September for the 2026 cycle because the most competitive states will face inventory pressure in October.
facts.quote: Book key inventory windows by early September.

facts.fact: For most 2026 competitive gubernatorial races, vendor says CTV at 55-65% of TV spend, broadcast at 30-40%, and cable at 5-10% is increasingly common.
facts.quote: For most 2026 competitive gubernatorial races, CTV at 55-65% of TV spend and broadcast at 30-40% (with cable at 5-10%) is increasingly common.

facts.fact: For open seats and challenger races in larger states, vendor says late spring (April-May) of the election year is typical for starting CTV.
facts.quote: For open seats and challenger races in larger states, late spring of the election year (April-May) is typical.

facts.fact: Vendor states most gubernatorial CTV spend concentrates in the August-November window, with the heaviest weight in the final 8 weeks.
facts.quote: The bulk of CTV spend in most gubernatorial races concentrates in the August-November window, with the heaviest weight in the final 8 weeks.

facts.fact: Vendor states the fastest October campaigns will use AI-assisted creative to push refreshes in 24-48 hours.
facts.quote: The campaigns moving fastest in October will use AI-assisted creative to push refreshes in 24-48 hours.

facts.fact: Vendor states Adwave is currently optimized for small business advertisers rather than political campaigns.
facts.quote: Adwave is currently optimized for small business advertisers rather than political campaigns.

facts.quote: Every campaign should have compliance counsel review CTV creative before launch.
